published_process_scope: Ohio Power Schedule DCT, 50–<100 MW fee bracket
what_to_prepare: Apply in PowerClerk with the specific location, load ramp and final load. Ohio Power requires control of the property through ownership, a lease or an option.
payment_timing_and_limits: An 80 MW request falls in the $50,000 one-time study fee bracket, payable within 45 days under the published process.
source_locator: Published application instructions and Load Study Fees

published_process_scope: Duquesne Light large-load transmission queue, form for loads over 5 MW
what_to_prepare: The transmission queue application calls for an executed deed, lease or purchase option, an electrical one-line and site plan stamped by a Pennsylvania-licensed engineer, and a 120-month load ramp. Add the data center questionnaire. A memorandum or document showing only intent to buy does not satisfy the published site-control requirement.
payment_timing_and_limits: Submit the signed study agreement and a $250,000 deposit with the queue application. The deposit funds study and engineering work. The utility says unused funds are returned if the project is canceled.
source_locator: Application step 2 and deposit FAQ. Data Request revision 01, sections 2 and 3.

published_process_scope: Dominion Energy Virginia data center feasibility and contracting process
what_to_prepare: Start the feasibility review with a site plan, load letter and ramp schedule. Dominion’s contracting report also calls for construction timing, meter delivery voltage and a breakdown of load by building where applicable. Confirm which land documents Dominion needs for the request.
payment_timing_and_limits: Dominion describes a $250,000 cash payment at signing of the Engineering Letter of Agreement, after feasibility review. Additional engineering can require further payment.
source_locator: Typical request steps. GS-5 Large-Load Rate Class Report, page 4.
